title: The Lanes at Union Market
name: TheLanesTenantAssociation
text:
Awful experience living here, both with Ranger Properties and then somehow even worse with HH Red Stone, a company that suddenly took over the property in summer 2026 and immediately tried to disregard the needs of and force out longer-term tenants who were not Howard students they could charge extravagant rent to.

In contrast to Ranger, who had polite and customer-service oriented upper management whenever there were problems with on-site staff, numerous corporate staff, including Gary Chen and Lexie Liu spoke to me on multiple occasions in language that can be considered demeaning, bullying and/or harassment.

While the front desk staff was often quick to admit that the HH corporate office (as a MD based company) didn't understand or follow DC housing law requirements and were more much reasonable to deal with on the rare occasion they were reachable, they were nonetheless overridden by a mgmt company that tried to (to my knowledge unlawfully) threaten residents with:

-unlawful rent notices / increases without 60 day standard notice
-long-term agreement reqs (dc is month-month after 12 months)
-threats to unilaterally end your lease or have police forcibly remove you off the priority (without a valid eviction order)
- withholding of (or charging excess security deposit fees w/o required justification to do so)
- interfered with protected tenant rights to organize (attempts to put up Tenant Association flyers were taken down on several occasions)
- bullying, intimidation and retaliation for exerting protected tenant rights, including the right to file complaints or pursue legal action
- similar discrimination against disabled residents for the above
- unfair rent renewal / discrimination practices  -  from speaking with various residents,we were all offered renewals at vastly different price ranges, ranging as low as a 0% to 40% increase.  No justifiable reason was given for the reason for these rent discrepancies, other than management to claim that the other tenants must be lying (despite residents sharing proof with one another directly).

Other housing condition and lease violations that occurred during my tenure:

- lack of hot water on a daily basis due to a poorly designed  boiler that seems to not heat all apartments equally (some too hot, others too cold)
- maintenance requests via the portal were often ignored, or entry would otherwise require without the required advance notice of entry
- missing window screens per dc statute
- zero evidence of effort to enforce "no smoking" clause in lease - emails and calls rarely returned, guards confirmed they were not told to enforce the rule on the roof
- constantly broken locks on external doors to building (security guards were hired due to improperly functioning doors without informing residents of the increased security risk)
- advertised features, such as the lobby bathroom and the external / direct access bike room were closed down during HH Red Stone takeover
- the leasing office rarely ever returned emails or phone calls and was often closed early without advance communication
- the front door lobby / security alarm went off frequently during 2025, sometimes for days at a time, without being effectively repaired (posing not only an annoyance but a security and fire alarm risk as the alarm was not properly functioning)
- despite advertising secure and accessible package retrieval, packages were often left stacked up in huge piles in and outside of the mailroom, making it exceptionally difficult to find or retrieve items on a daily basis.
- delivery people and guests were unable to easily use the intercom or keypad for building access, which often went offline and required going down to the lobby door to retrieve guests
- physical Latch keys promised to longer-term residents were taken away without notice, posing a challenge visually limited residents/guests
- advertised WiFi constantly went out and was unreliable
- 24 hour emergency # often not working or not answered

Please email (see full Gmail name above) if a resident interested in class action

title: The Lanes at Union Market
name: Meagan j
text:
The Lanes is a home away from home. The complex is a modern building with floor-to-ceiling windows that offer an amazing view overlooking Union Market. My room is a great size (about 300 square feet) in a three-bedroom, two-bath apartment, and the bed frame comfortably fits a queen or full-size bed. There is a 24-hour laundry room downstairs that gets the job done, which is super convenient.

The rooftop is truly breathtaking, especially if you value views. You can see the entire landscape of Florida Avenue, which is aesthetically pleasing particularly at night.

Most importantly, the management office is extremely attentive to tenants’ needs and always available when a situation needs attention. They have a super friendly personality and are always ready to help, which really makes a difference in the overall living experience.

title: The Lanes at Union Market
name: TR
text:
Edit: Update after living in the building for a full year after HH Red Stone takeover:

Despite a semi-promising start in some areas, new management has somehow run the building into the ground even further for those of us who are not students and might not care.

The elevators never work, the A/C has had problems all summer, they have tried to close the roof almost ALL summer due to broken A/C, despite both the terrace and gym being there.  The front door building alarm constantly goes off, laundry room is often flooded.  They blame all problems on old
management and claim they don't have responsibility in fixing it. Aside from Sheyth, they don't answer calls or emails.   Stay far away!

--

Warning to prospective tenants: the building is undergoing foreclosure on May 23.   Hopefully future residents will hopefully be dealing with a much more honest, transparent and reliable property management team, as well as a new building engineer and on-site support staff who are nicer and more responsive to resident needs, but that is most definitely not the case as of right now.

The majority of the 5 star reviews on here are left by old property management and their employees/affiliates, so please take them with a grain of salt.

Note: The news about the foreclosure is a fact I only found out from other residents and local news, not through property management itself.  I’m in touch with residents still there who have confirmed there’s been a decline (if that’s even possible?) of management response since a new manager came in in early May.

I would personally suggest any prospective tenants wait at least 4-6 months before moving in, so that a new team is fully operating and has made the necessary improvements so that you do not run into these same issues in your own experience.

I had to move out of the Lanes due to a huge and impractical rent hike, and the knowledge I have been paying significantly more than some other residents have been able to negotiate thus far.

Warning to new residents: do not get lured in with any offers of concessions unless you can afford a several hundred dollar increase in rent.

The rent hike might have been justified if the management delivered on any of their promises made to residents prior to or upon move-in, but as other tenants have noted: many of the promises such as free inclusive wifi were not honored, and many other advertised services such as an on-site management team, community events, rule enforcement and maintenance of the common areas has been non-existent the majority of the time I’ve been here.

Michael Stower, the building engineer / maintenance guy is the only on-site staff member and as other reviews on here have already mentioned, the majority of the time he was very slow and unresponsive to maintenance requests, and tends be extremely rude and dismissive when you try to follow-up with him or point out mistakes.  He often acts like he’s doing YOU a huge favor by doing a job he’s paid for, and doesn’t seem to know the first thing about providing customer service to paying tenants, or being a responsible professional even when he is stressed out (which is at least 99% of the time).

He struggles to keep up with electronic communication through any platform and insists on residents always call him on the phone, despite not being able to keep up with or remember these phone call requests either. There have been several times when he has hung up on or threatened to block myself and several other tenants on his phone or the portal MaintainX.

The old property manager is remote (based in NY) and often used that or the lack of onsite staff to justify being able to resolve resident complaints and concerns.

The new manager that came in early May was equally non-communicative prior to my departure, even in urgent situations (such as when the elevators went out for 2 days), and has sadly decided it was appropriate to give Michael a promotion, despite numerous negative reviews and complaints about his interpersonal skills and maintenance performance.

—

title: The Lanes at Union Market
name: Clare Driscoll
text: I would not recommend living in this building to anyone. It has been two months since I moved out of my apartment and I have yet to receive my security deposit. Per D.C. law, the security deposit must be refunded within a 45 day period and it is not well beyond that. When I have tried to inquire about the status of my refund to the leasing office I receive short, vague responses or, most of the time, no response at all. The lack of communication from the leasing office is highly unprofessional, and was a consistent theme while I lived here. I have sent a complaint in to the corporate office to hope they can resolve the mishandling of this situation.

title: The Lanes at Union Market
name: Maya Holcomb
text:
It has been four months since I moved out and I have yet to receive my security deposit. Not only does this break DC law requiring the deposit be returned within 45 days of move out, but it means I’m short a full month’s rent. The Office of the Tenant Advocate, Office of the Attorney General, and my constituent services staff have all been helpful in navigating this process. Aside from the poor quality building, overpriced rent, and inadequate internet (despite advertised free Wi-Fi), the building has been incredibly challenging to work with.

In addition to breaking DC Code by not returning my security deposit of 1 month’s rent, the lease also required for 60 day notice intent to vacate which breaks DC law requiring no more than 30 days. Overall, the leasing practices are disingenuous.

* Michael Stowers is the one exception to my poor experience. He is efficient, helpful, and does a great job with upkeep of maintenance. He takes his time solving problems with care, even though he is a one man team responsible for maintenance for the full building.

title: The Lanes at Union Market

text:

If there is a new landlord they are unreachable, like previous management, and only seem to care about making more $$$ rather than resident satisfaction..

I recently found out I was overpaying compared to other residents (many of whom have been offered a second year lease at the same rate as their first year). I’ve been trying to break my lease and there’s no response from management.

title: The Lanes at Union Market
name: Jess Thompson
text: My experience at The Lanes was nothing short of disappointing. First and foremost, the maintenance of the building left much to be desired. The rooftop was often left uncleaned (sometimes bordering gross). Tenants were promised physical entry key cards that were never delivered. The windows in the bedrooms were not fully functional. Additionally, during my stay, the wifi was out for over a month. Free wifi was listed as an amenity at the property and when the outage occurred, management recommended tenants set up their own wifi service. Tenants (many of whom are students) were drawn in with promises of free wifi to only be told they are out of luck and need to set up their own account. Further, tenants did not receive appropriate communication during this outage, receiving minimal emails and almost no updates. The property manager is not on-site. I believe he is in New York full time. The leasing agent is a contractor and cannot help with building issues. The maintenance engineer, who is the only on-site employee, was often rude and dismissive. Overall, I would not recommend living at this property. As others have commented, there are similarly priced buildings in the area with far better management.
